IS-Bench robot-scene constraints:
- The image is from a robot first-person camera in simulation.
- Do not label the robot arm, gripper, or tool as a human hand or person.
- Only use hand_left, hand_right, or person if an actual human body part is visible.
- A closed task object list is appended to this prompt at runtime. It overrides
  every earlier open-vocabulary naming example: emit an object only when it is
  visibly present and its `name` is exactly one item in that appended list. Do
  not use synonyms, aliases, plurals, instance suffixes, or task-external scene
  objects. The robot itself is never a scene-graph object.
- Before producing JSON for every frame, perform two deliberate visual passes.
  First scan the full image for the visible scene layout, supports, and
  containers. Then make a mandatory exhaustive verification pass over the
  closed task object list and every visible support surface. In that second
  pass, inspect table/counter edges, centers, and partially covered regions for
  any visible instance with special attention to small, thin, flat, elongated,
  transparent, background-blending, or partially occluded objects. This second
  pass is required even when there is no navigation target. Emit one node for
  every physically distinct instance with visible pixels; do not omit one
  because it is less salient than a larger nearby object. Do not invent an
  object when no part of it is visible.
- Every object emitted for this frame must include `"is_vis": true`. Do not
  infer hidden, occluded, historical, or merely task-mentioned objects.
- Emit relationships only between listed visible objects. `predicate` must be
  exactly one of: `on`, `in`, `above`, `attach to`, `near`.
  - `on`: the subject is directly supported by or resting on the object.
  - `in`: the subject is inside or contained by the object.
  - `above`: the subject is vertically higher without claiming contact.
  - `attach to`: the subject is physically connected or fastened to the object.
  - `near`: the subject is spatially close without support, containment, or
    attachment.
- Do not output an edge when the relationship is uncertain. Do not reverse an
  `in` or `on` edge: the movable/contained subject is `subj_id`, and its
  container or support is `obj_id`.
- For two large support or room objects, use only `near`. For a small object
  and a large support or container, use `on`, `in`, or `above` from the small
  object toward the large object. Use `attach to` or `near` between two small
  objects only when the image clearly supports it.
